title: Dussehra to Diwali: India's Festival Season in Numbers
sourceShort: Official data: Consumer Affairs, MoSPI, NDDB, VAHAN, RBI, India Post, Metro Railway Kolkata, PIB
source: Department of Consumer Affairs: daily all-India average retail prices, 16 Oct 2026 (fcainfoweb.nic.in). MoSPI: Consumer Price Index (base 2024), September 2026, provisional (eSankhyiki). NDDB: per capita availability of milk by state, from Basic Animal Husbandry Statistics. MoRTH: VAHAN public dashboard, read 17 Oct 2026. Reserve Bank of India: Holiday Matrix, October 2026; RBI Bulletin, September 2026 and November 2025. Department of Posts: holidays list 2026. Metro Railway, Kolkata: press releases of 28 Sep and 3 Oct 2025. Cabinet: Productivity Linked Bonus, PIB, 14 Oct 2026.

vo.text: Onion costs ninety-six percent more than a year ago, and on India Post's all-India list, Diwali falls on a Sunday.
Here is the festival season in official numbers: dates, kitchen prices, sweets, vehicles, travel and cash.

scenes.title: The calendar
scenes.sub: Festival days from Dussehra to Christmas, on India Post's list

vo.text: First, the calendar.

scenes.source: Department of Posts · holidays list 2026, All India and circle tabs · indiapost.gov.in, read 17 Oct 2026
scenes.title: India Post's holiday list for 2026
scenes.note: Dussehra Tue 20 Oct · Diwali Sun 8 Nov · Chhath Mon 16 Nov (Bihar) · Guru Nanak's birthday Tue 24 Nov · Christmas Fri 25 Dec

tiles.caption: of them on a Sunday: Diwali, 8 Nov
of 31 circle lists also mark Monday 19 Oct

vo.text: The dates, from India Post's all-India list: Dussehra on Tuesday, the twentieth of October.
Diwali on Sunday, the eighth of November, nineteen days later.
Chhath in Bihar on the sixteenth, Guru Nanak's birthday on the twenty-fourth, and Christmas on Friday the twenty-fifth.
In thirteen of the thirty-one circle lists on India Post's page, Monday the nineteenth is also a holiday.

scenes.source: Reserve Bank of India · Holiday Matrix, October 2026 · rbi.org.in, read 17 Oct 2026
scenes.title: Bank holidays in October 2026: RBI offices with four or more, and two metros
scenes.caption: Holidays the RBI lists for each of its 34 offices. Sundays and second and fourth Saturdays are bank holidays everywhere; the Kolkata and Bengaluru lists include Saturday 10 Oct.

vo.text: The Reserve Bank publishes a holiday list for each of its offices.
In October it showed six at Agartala and five at Kolkata, against two each at Mumbai and New Delhi.

scenes.title: The kitchen
scenes.sub: Prices on the same date, three years running

vo.text: Next, the kitchen.

scenes.source: Department of Consumer Affairs · daily retail prices, all-India average · 16 Oct 2026
scenes.title: Onion, a kilo: all-India average retail price
scenes.caption: Up 96% in a year. Two years earlier, on 16 Oct 2024: ₹54.73.

vo.text: Every day, the Consumer Affairs department publishes the average retail price of essentials across India.
On the sixteenth of October, a kilo of onion cost fifty-two rupees and seventy paise.
A year earlier, it was twenty-six rupees and eighty-eight paise. This year's price is ninety-six percent higher.
On the same date two years ago: fifty-four rupees and seventy-three paise.

scenes.source: Department of Consumer Affairs · daily retail prices, all-India average · 16 Oct 2026
scenes.title: Price change in one year, selected kitchen items, to 16 Oct 2026
scenes.caption: All-India average retail prices on 16 Oct 2026 against 16 Oct 2025. Nine of the items the department prices daily.

vo.text: Here is the change over one year for some festival kitchen items.
Sugar is up twenty-four percent, jaggery fifteen percent, and tur dal fourteen percent.
Mustard oil is up nine percent, desi ghee six percent, and milk four percent.
A kilo of sugar now costs fifty-seven rupees and eighty-two paise.

scenes.source: Department of Consumer Affairs · daily retail prices, all-India average · 16 Oct 2026
scenes.title: Cheaper than two years ago
scenes.note: A year earlier, on 16 Oct 2025: potato ₹25.38, tomato ₹38.65.

vo.text: Two vegetables cost less than two years ago.
Potato, at twenty-two rupees and sixty-five paise, is cheaper than a year ago too.
Tomato, at forty rupees and seventy-four paise, is slightly higher than last year.
Two years ago, it cost sixty-seven rupees and ninety-six paise.

scenes.title: Sweets and milk
scenes.sub: Sugar, sweets and the milk behind them

vo.text: Then, sweets and milk.

scenes.source: MoSPI · CPI (base 2024), all-India items · Sep 2026 provisional · eSankhyiki portal
scenes.title: Price rise in a year, September 2026: consumer price index
scenes.caption: The Statistics Ministry's index, base 2024, September 2026 against September 2025, provisional. It measures prices differently from the daily retail figures.

vo.text: Next, sweets, in the Statistics Ministry's price index.
Ready-made sweets, with milk or without, cost nine point four percent more this September than last.
Sugar in this index: twenty-nine point eight percent.
The index measures prices differently from the daily retail figures, so the two sugar numbers differ.

scenes.source: NDDB · per capita availability of milk by state, from Basic Animal Husbandry Statistics · nddb.coop
scenes.title: Milk produced per person per day, year to March 2024
scenes.sub: India 471 g · grams a day, by state
scenes.note: Milk produced in a state, divided by its people: not what people drink. Dadra and Nagar Haveli is not shown.

vo.text: Milk goes into many of those sweets. Which state produces the most milk per person?
Punjab: one thousand two hundred and forty-five grams a day, in the year to March twenty twenty-four.
This counts milk produced, divided by population. It is not what people drink.
Then Rajasthan, one thousand one hundred and seventy-one grams, and Haryana, one thousand one hundred and five grams.
India as a whole: four hundred and seventy-one grams.
The lowest: Lakshadweep, fifteen grams, and Arunachal Pradesh, thirty-five grams.
Now, vehicles.

scenes.source: MoRTH · VAHAN public dashboard · read 17 Oct 2026 · Diwali 2025: PIB, 20 Oct 2025
scenes.title: Vehicles registered in India, by month
scenes.caption: All vehicle classes, VAHAN dashboard, read 17 Oct 2026; October 2026 was not over. Diwali was on 20 Oct in 2025, and is on 8 Nov in 2026.

vo.text: In September twenty twenty-five, nineteen point three one lakh vehicles were registered across India.
In October, forty-one point seven lakh: more than double.
That was forty-two percent more than in October twenty twenty-four, by our arithmetic.
Diwali fell in October last year. This year it falls in November.
As of the seventeenth, this October's count stood at eleven point seven one lakh. The month was not over.

scenes.title: Journeys home
scenes.sub: Fares, and Durga Puja on the Kolkata Metro

vo.text: Next, travel.

scenes.source: MoSPI · CPI (base 2024), all-India items · Sep 2026 provisional · eSankhyiki portal
scenes.title: Fares, price rise in a year, September 2026
scenes.caption: The Statistics Ministry's consumer price index, base 2024, September 2026, provisional.

vo.text: Air fares in the Statistics Ministry's index were twenty-nine point nine percent higher in September than a year before.
Bus fares for occasional trips rose four point one percent, and rail fares two point two percent.

scenes.source: Metro Railway, Kolkata · press releases of 28 Sep and 3 Oct 2025
scenes.title: Kolkata Metro at Durga Puja
scenes.note: Panchami to Dashami, 2024: 41.15 lakh. Metro Railway had issued no 2026 Puja figures when this was made.

tiles.caption: more than this on Maha Panchami 2025: a one-day record then

vo.text: Take one city.
Last year on Maha Panchami, the Kolkata Metro carried more than nine point eight two lakh, a one-day record then.
The earlier record was nine point six one lakh, in twenty twenty-four.
From Panchami to Dashami, forty-six point five six lakh rode, against forty-one point one five lakh a year before.
And money.

scenes.source: Reserve Bank of India · RBI Bulletin, State of the Economy, September 2026 and November 2025
scenes.title: Currency in circulation, growth over a year
scenes.caption: 13.2% on 15 Sep 2026, from 12.4% on 15 Aug. The RBI: the highest print in five years.

b.label: 15 Sep 2026
b.sub: the latest in the RBI Bulletin

vo.text: The RBI reports how fast currency in circulation is growing, year on year.
On the fifteenth of September, growth was thirteen point two percent.
The month before, it was twelve point four percent. The RBI calls the September figure the highest in five years.
In mid-October last year, growth was eight point eight percent.

scenes.source: Reserve Bank of India · RBI Bulletin, November 2025, State of the Economy · rbi.org.in
scenes.text: The moderation of growth in currency in circulation was primarily due to the waning of festive demand.
scenes.by: Reserve Bank of India, RBI Bulletin, November 2025

vo.text: By mid-November last year, growth had eased to eight point one percent.
The RBI's Bulletin put that down to waning festive demand.

scenes.source: Cabinet · Productivity Linked Bonus for railway employees · PIB, 14 Oct 2026
scenes.title: Railway staff bonus, approved 14 Oct 2026
scenes.note: Cabinet decision of 14 Oct 2026, as released by PIB.

tiles.caption: the most one person can get

vo.text: On the fourteenth of October, the Cabinet approved a bonus for railway staff: seventy-eight days' wages.
The total is two thousand and nine point six one crore rupees, for about eleven point four lakh eligible staff.
The most any one person can get is seventeen thousand nine hundred and fifty-one rupees.
The release says it is paid each year before the Durga Puja and Dussehra holidays.

tiles.caption: onion retail price, in a year, to 16 Oct
sugar retail price, in a year, to 16 Oct
growth of currency in circulation, 15 Sep 2026

vo.text: So: onion up ninety-six percent in a year and sugar up twenty-four percent, by the daily retail figures.
Last October, more than twice September's vehicle registrations.
And growth in currency in circulation at a five-year high, the RBI says.
